text_translated_detailed: Wednesday the 11th of July 1742. Present all except the gentlemen Helvelius and the Water Fiscal, the latter through indisposition. — By the noble gentleman president Mr. Jacob Lakeman brought before the council was the following Extract, reading as follows: Extract from the Minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India on Thursday the 5th of July in the year 1742. At the most recent assembly, after resumption of an incoming minute from the esteemed council of Justice of this castle, dated the 3rd current, together with two authenticated copies of opinions concerning the requests made by the former gentleman Governor-General Valckenier with respect to the recollections noted, the disposition regarding the members in the aforementioned court of justice, who in the said recollection had agreed to this convocation being examined, it was then by the gentleman Governor-General placed before the gentlemen councillors for consideration whether one should not now proceed to the fulfillment of the aforementioned command of the High Noble gentlemen Seventeen, and as this was deemed necessary, it was resolved good to order the ordinary members in the aforementioned college, Mr. Bernhard Jacob Dellafaille, Mr. Pieter Willem Lammens, Mr. Theodorus Policarpus Woit, and the extraordinary member Mr. Jan Blocquau, pursuant to the letter of the aforementioned noble gentlemen of the 13th of December of the past year, to refrain from all legal proceedings and judicature that shall fall to them in the matter of the former gentleman Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier. And hereupon it was further understood that the remaining members of that College who in the aforementioned recollection had not agreed, and consist of the ordinary members, Mr. Jacob van den Bosch, Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst, Mr. Reijnier Stapel, together with the two newly arrived members Mr. Jacob Pompe van Meerdervoort and Mr. Philippus Rochus Kien in that court regarding the aforementioned affairs, without prejudice to the right of the parties to maintain their seats

text_original: Woensdag den 11:' Iulij A:o 1742. Present den Edelen heere President, Item de verdere heeren Raaden en g'assumeerde leeden in desen. door den Edelen heere Preesident deses raads m:r Jacob Lakeman, din raade overgebragt zijnde, een Extract uijt de notulen van 't gebesoigneerde en geresolveerde in raade van Jndia, genomen op den 5:' deser, en daar bij gebleken zijnde, hoe haar Hoog Edelens ingevolge het aanschrijvens van de hoog Edele Heeren Seventienen hadden gelast de heeren m:r Bernhard Iacob Dellafaille, Pieter Willem Lammens, Theodorus Polijcarpus Woijt en Jan Blocquau, hun van alle regtspleging, en Judica „tuure in deeser zaake van den gewesene heere gouverneur generaal adriaan Valckenier te vallen, te onthouden en in dezelven plaatse wederom te assumeeren als leeden in voorm:te zaak, den boekhouder generaal Evert christoffel Lanius, en den capitain militair Rudolph caxel von glan, met de kooplieden Ian Cornelis Duquesne, en Corijn Steevensz. die dan ook „ ordre van gem: edelen heere president boven gekomen, en in raade verscheenen zijnde, den Eed tot het ampt van raad van Justitie staende in handen van welgem: Edelen heere president afgelegt, en door sijn Edele, en de overige leeden deses raads, ingevolge het geordonneerde van haar Ed=le hoog agtb: den selven Eed vernieuwt hebben, na het welk het secreet aanschrijvens van haar Edele hoog agtb: aan de Edele hooge regeering deser landen, van dato 13:' december 1741. opgelesen, en daar op den heer advocaat fiscaal m:r Cornelis Phillip die in tusschen in de vertrek kamer was versogt te gaan binnen gerequireert zynde, wierd na de ordre van welgemelde Haar Edele Hoog agtb sijn E: bij desen raade bij provisie van sijn ampt gesuspendeert, en den heer waterfiscaal m:r Jan hendrik van Panhuijs, die versogt was boven te komen, als doen geordonneert, alle dagelijkse voorvallende zaaken„ het ampt van advocaat fiscaal
text_translated_detailed: Wednesday the 11th of July in the year 1742. Present the noble gentleman President, likewise the further gentlemen Councillors and assumed members herein. By the noble gentleman President of this council Mr. Jacob Lakeman brought before the council was an Extract from the minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India, taken on the 5th of this month, and thereby it appeared how their High Excellencies, pursuant to the letter of the High Noble gentlemen Seventeen, had ordered the gentlemen Mr. Bernhard Jacob Dellafaille, Pieter Willem Lammens, Theodorus Policarpus Woit and Jan Blocquau to refrain from all legal proceedings and judicature falling to them in the matter of the former gentleman Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, and in their place again to assume as members in the aforementioned matter, the general bookkeeper Evert Christoffel Lanius and the military captain Rudolph Caxel von Glan, together with the merchants Jan Cornelis Duquesne and Corijn Steevensz. Who then also, by order of the aforementioned noble gentleman president having come above and appeared in council, took the oath for the office of councillor of Justice standing in the hands of the aforementioned noble gentleman president, and by his Excellency and the remaining members of this council, pursuant to the ordinance of their Excellencies the High Esteemed, renewed the same oath. After which the secret letter of their Excellency the High Esteemed to the noble high government of these lands, dated the 13th of December 1741, was read aloud, and thereupon the gentleman advocate fiscal Mr. Cornelis Phillip, who in the meantime had been requested to go to the antechamber, being called back, was by order of the aforementioned their Excellency the High Esteemed by this council provisionally suspended from his office, and the gentleman water fiscal Mr. Jan Hendrik van Panhuijs, who had been requested to come up, was then ordered to attend to all daily occurring matters regarding the office of advocate fiscal

text_original: Saturdag den 14:e Iulij Ao 1742 Present den Edelen heere President Item de verdere heeren Raaden, en geassumeerde leden in desen door den Ed:e heere president m:r Jacob lakeman is op heden overgebragt het na volgende, Extract uijt de notulen van 't gebesoigneerde en Geresolveerde in rade van India weg Vrijdag den 13:' Julij 1742. Wijders is na resumtie van voorsz: ingekomen notul van den agtb: raad van Justitie deses Casteels van den 11:' deser verstaan, haar Agtb: te recommandeeren, om met het verder gedemandeerde door haar Edele hoog Agtb: de heeren Seventhienen in't Patria bij missiven van den 23:' 7br: 10. 8ber en 13:' xber d' anno pass:o voort te gaan, /onderstont:/ accordeert / was getekent./ P:s A:s v. d parra sec=s„ Na welkers resumptie door den Edelen heere praesident de novo sijnde opgelesen het speciaal genoteerde bij haar Edele hoog agtb: geeerde secrete missive van dato 13:' xber 1741. conserneerende d' aanstelling door desen raade van een Fiscaal prointerim instede van de heer M:r Cornelis Phillips zoo wierd alverder door wel gem sijn Ed: en sulx na de intentie van haar Edele hoog agtb: aan de permanente heeren leeden affgevraagd off ook een van hun E:s dit ampt van fiscaal provisioneel ten dienste der Justitie wilde op sig neemen, en daar op door d' Vier voorsettende heeren leeden m:r Jacob van den Bosch, M:r Theodorus van Reverhorst, m:r Reijnier Stapel, en M:r Iacob Pompe van meerdervoort, verklaart zijnde geensints daer toe geinclinee te sijn, heeft de heer m:r Philippus Rochus Kien versogt, dat sijn E: alvoorens sig daar op te verklaren mogte hebben den tijd van driemaal vier en twintig, dan wel tot aanstaende Woensdag, om als dan sig dierwegen frnaal te declareeren, 't geene dan ook na gedane om vrage bij desen rade aan sijn E: geaccordeert
text_translated_detailed: Saturday the 14th of July in the year 1742. Present: the Noble Lord President, and furthermore the other gentlemen Councillors and co-opted members herein. By the Honorable Lord President, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, there was presented today the following extract from the minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India on Friday the 13th of July 1742. Furthermore, upon resumption of the aforementioned incoming minute from the esteemed Council of Justice of this Castle of the 11th of this month, it was understood that their Esteemed Excellency should be recommended to proceed further with what was demanded by their Noble High Excellency the gentlemen Seventeen in the Fatherland by missives of the 23rd of September, 10th of October, and 13th of December of the past year, /understood:/ agreed /was signed./ P.s A.s v. d. parra sec.s. After whose resumption, by the Noble Lord President, the special notation made by their Noble High Excellency in their esteemed secret missive of the date 13th of December 1741, concerning the appointment by this Council of a Fiscal pro interim in place of the gentleman Mr. Cornelis Phillips, was read anew. Thus it was further asked by the aforementioned Honorable Lord President, and in accordance with the intention of their Noble High Excellency, of the permanent gentlemen members whether one of their Excellencies would be willing to take upon himself this office of Fiscal provisionally in service of Justice. And when the four presiding gentlemen members, Mr. Jacob van den Bosch, Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst, Mr. Reijnier Stapel, and Mr. Jacob Pompe van Meerdervoort, declared themselves not at all inclined to do so, the gentleman Mr. Philippus Rochus Kien requested that his Excellency, before declaring himself thereupon, might have the time of three times twenty-four hours, or else until the coming Wednesday, so that he might then declare himself in this matter finally. This was then also, after inquiry made by this Council to his Excellency, granted to him.

text_translated_detailed: Saturday the 14th of July 1742. Present: the Noble Lord President, and the gentlemen Councillors and co-opted members herein. It having been taken into consideration by this Council how the clerk Clercq Paul Fredrik Eversoon, according to his declaration made, to be found in the minute of the 11th of December 1741, had delivered to the gentleman Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius the documents and papers which, at the request of the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, had been sworn to with their respective annotations placed behind them, and this without the least prior knowledge or qualification of the Council or of the Commissioners who had exercised oversight over those same annotations. Thus it was deemed good that the secretary of this Council be ordered to command the aforementioned clerk Clercq Eversoon from now onwards, in the matter concerning the former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, not to be employed with the consequences and undertakings thereof, or to allow the same to authenticate any papers concerning this, but this requiring, as then, the adjunct clerk Clercq Pieter Haksteen to be used. /:Understood:/ in acknowledgment of me, as I have been specially requested hereto. En Stevens. S. /was signed:/ Extracted from the memorial of the esteemed Council of Justice of this Castle and agreed upon. Batavia, dated as above. Baksteen, Adv. Gesw. Clercq. Saturday the 14th of July in the year 1742. Present: the Noble Lord President, and furthermore the other gentlemen Councillors and co-opted members herein. The bailiff Pieter Boockesteijn, who, in accordance with the ordinance of their Noble High Excellency the gentlemen Seventeen, by their Noble High Excellency's esteemed secret missive of the date 13th of December 1741, just as well as the advocate fiscal Mr. Cornelis Phillips, was to be suspended from this Council by provision of his office, having some time ago come to pass away, it is hereby understood by this Council to keep this note thereof. /Understood:/ in acknowledgment of me/ was signed. G.s Schuijlenburg, secretary.

G'extraheert uijt het memoriaal van den agtb raad van justitie deses Casteels en accordeert Batavia Datum utsupra H Haksteen adv„t Gesw: Clercq N:o 7 Woensdag den 18:' Iulij 1742 Present den Edelen heere President Item de heeren raden en geassumeerde leeden in desen Jngevolge het genotuleerde van den 14:' deser door d' heer m:r Phillippus Rochus Okien aangenomen sijnde sig op heeden te declareeren off zijn E het ampt van fiscaal prointerim 't geen sijn E: nevens de andere permanente heeren leeden was opgedragen, soude gelieve op sig te neemen, dan niet, soo heeft als nu gem: heer Kien verklaard na alvovens, het een en ander rijpelijk te hebben overwogen, daer van ten eenemael aff te sien en geensints daer toe geinclineert te zijn, wanneer daar op door den Ed: heere president m=r Jacob Lakeman aan de heeren leeden gevraagt wesende off haar E=s na volgens het bereets aangetekende ter notule voorm: haare gedagten hadde laten gaan op een bequaamen kundig persoon aan wien men dit fiscaplaat prointerim met gerustheijd soude kunnen toevertrouwen en daar op in consideratie gekomen zijnde m:r Nicolaas Iongsma die niet alleen in regten ervaren, en gepromoveert, maar ook in Vriesland en alhier de practijcq eenigen tijd g'Exerceert mitsgaders het ampt van secretaris van Heeren scheepenen deser steede heeft waargenomen gehad
text_translated_detailed: Wednesday the 10th of July in the year 1742. Present were all except the gentlemen de la Saille, Pompe van Meerdervoort, and the water fiscal. By the noble gentleman president of this council, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, it was communicated in council today that the gentleman advocate fiscal, Mr. Cornelis Phillips, on the most recent Wednesday, in accordance with the express order and the written directive of the gentlemen majors in the homeland, had been suspended from his office provisionally. It was deemed good to keep record of this, undersigned, in knowledge of me, was signed P.L. F. Eversoon, sworn clerk. Extracted from the memorial of the venerable council of justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, dated as above. H. Haksteen, advocate, sworn clerk. No. 7. Wednesday the 18th of July 1742. Present the noble gentleman President. Also the gentlemen councilors and co-opted members herein. In accordance with what was noted on the 14th of this month, Mr. Philippus Rochus Okien having been approached, was asked to declare today whether His Excellency would be pleased to assume the office of fiscal pro interim, which His Excellency, along with the other permanent members, had been assigned. Or not. So the aforementioned gentleman Kien has now declared, after having thoroughly considered the matter in all respects, to refrain entirely from it and to be in no way inclined to do so. Whereupon the noble gentleman president, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, asked the gentlemen members whether Their Excellencies, according to what had already been noted in the aforementioned minutes, had given thought to a suitable and capable person to whom this fiscal position pro interim could be entrusted with confidence. And upon consideration, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma came into consideration, who is not only experienced in law and has been promoted, but has also practiced for some time in Friesland and here, and has moreover held the office of secretary of the gentlemen aldermen of this city.

text_translated_detailed: Thursday the 19th of July 1742. Present were all except the gentlemen Helvetius and Lammens, both through indisposition. By the noble gentleman president, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, it was made known to the council that on yesterday, in accordance with the written directive of the High Excellencies, the gentlemen Seventeen, by their secret missive dated the 13th of December 1741, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma as advocate fiscal of India pro interim was appointed by this council, and that His Excellency, in order to be sworn in that office, was ordered to come up today. As when the co-opted members of this council and together with the aforementioned Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, who had meanwhile waited a little in the adjoining chamber, were brought in. So the aforementioned Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma took the oath for the office of advocate fiscal, standing in the hands of the well-born noble gentleman president. After which the gentleman water fiscal, Mr. Jan Hendrik van Panhuijs, was requested to hand over the two constables, together with the lesser servants of Justice who belong to the land fiscal's office, to the newly appointed pro interim officer, together with the aforementioned constables. And the servants of this council were called in, and the appointment of the aforementioned Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma as pro interim advocate fiscal was announced to them. So it was further understood that record of this be kept. Undersigned, in knowledge of me, was signed G.S. Schuylenburg. Extracted from the memorial of the venerable secrets council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, dated as above. Haksteen, adjunct, sworn clerk. Thursday the 19th of July 1742. text_translated_detailed: Monday the 23rd of July 1742. Present the Noble Lord President, as well as the gentlemen Councillors, and assumed members in this matter, including the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal. Today, by the Noble Lord President Mr. Jacob Lakeman, the meeting having been expressly convened in order to attend to and carefully deliberate how and in what manner one might best and most appropriately cause the points demanded by Your Excellencies the Noble and Highly Esteemed Gentlemen the Seventeen, both by common and secret missive dated the 23rd of September and 13th of December 1741, addressed to this Council, insofar as the Inquiry is concerned, to take effect, and to be put into operation according to the desire of Your Excellencies the Noble and Highly Esteemed; and thereupon the aforementioned orders of Your Excellencies the Noble and Highly Esteemed having been read anew, it was understood after consideration of what was necessary by this Council, first of all to have delivered to the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma an authenticated copy of such three Extracts from the letter of Your Excellencies the Noble and Highly Esteemed aforementioned, as were brought before this Council by the Noble Lord President on the 11th of this month, to the end that by the said Pro interim Advocate Fiscal such use thereof might be made, and means put into operation, as His Excellency shall deem and find necessary and fitting for the obtaining of the necessary information for the right of the high authority and the true interest of the Company's office, and by duty; in order to have all of these convened before the gentlemen commissioners from this Council together with the adjunct sworn clerk, and to that end by the Noble Lord President to commit two members every eight days, who shall each time make report of their proceedings at the next meeting; understood, in knowledge of me was signed G. ' november 1741. text_translated_detailed: No. 13, 1742, on the 4th of August, I, the undersigned, at the order of the well-esteemed gentleman president Mr. Jacob Lakeman, proceeded further to the house of the well-esteemed gentleman Nicolaes Crul, as first authorized representative of the former gentleman governor-general Adriaan Valckenier, for the purpose of, in accordance with the disposition of the first of this month by the esteemed council of justice, demanding such specification of goods, effects, and monies as are held by their excellencies from the aforementioned gentleman governor-general Valckenier, when by his excellency upon my service of process there was handed to me an original memorandum under date the 2nd with its amplification dated the 5th of November 1741, signed in his own hand by the aforementioned gentleman governor-general and his three authorized representatives, and then also eight copies of extracts of the sold loose and fixed goods signed by the current auctioneer Jan van Polanen, in order to be able to see from this the amount thereof which stands open in blank in the said memorandum; furthermore his excellency's answer in writing reads word for word as follows: "that there are no monies, goods, or effects held by the authorized representatives Helvitius and van der Linden, but indeed the papers are with the gentleman Helvitius, that under the authorized representative Nicolaes Crul likewise no goods or effects are held, but indeed the monies belonging to the gentleman Valckenier, to the amount of seventy-nine thousand two hundred sixty-six rixdollars and four stivers [modern equivalent: Dutch currency subdivision], namely as authorized representatives therefore outside or apart from the forty thousand rixdollars as debtor, and by the memorandum expressed in full, namely rixdollars 79266:4.—, furthermore that by the authorized representatives in the least no monies have been transferred to the gentleman Valckenier nor also not for his account to anyone else whoever it might be. His excellency requested the memorandum, amplification, and extracts.

text_original: N:o: 25. Woensdag den 12„' Septemb 1742. Present den Edelen heer praesident item de heeren Raaden ende g'assumeerde Lieeden in desen, Excepto de heer stevens. door den heer prointerim advocalt fiscael van india m„r Nicolaes Iongsma aan desen raede zijnde te kennen gegeven dat sijn E: van den secretaris deses raads gijsbertus Schuijlenburg in Copia hadde gevordert de notulen van haer hoog Ed: en daer op gevolgde besluijten van desen raede van datis 3. 11. en 18. julij deses jaers gevollen dog dat hij secretaris swaerigheijt hadde gemaekt die aan sijn E: buijten voor kennisse van desen raede aftegeven versoekende mitsdien dat zijn E. soo weel al zijne predecesseurs mag gaureeren van zoodanige notue als op den 12:' Janu: 1735 bij desen raede is genomen waer bij den advocaet fisc:l is geaccordeert visie en Copia van alle soodanige stucken als den selve in zijn ampt mogte benodigt zijn en mitsdien dat den secretaris mag werden geordonn:t de gerequireerde Copijen dewedes zijn E: uijt kragt van voors notul de dato 12:' Janu: 1735. te doen geworden als deselve Exofficio benodigt zijnde
text_translated_detailed: No. 25. Wednesday, the 12th of September 1742. Present: the esteemed Lord President, and the Lords Councillors and co-opted members herein, excepting the Lord Stevens. By the Lord pro-interim advocate fiscal of India, Mr. Nicolaes Jongsma, it was made known to this Council that His Excellency had requested from the secretary of this Council, Gijsbertus Schuijlenburg, in copy, the minutes of their High Excellencies and the resolutions of this Council following thereupon, dated the 3rd, 11th, and 18th of July of this year, but that the secretary had made difficulties about providing them to His Excellency outside the knowledge of this Council. Requesting therefore that His Excellency, as well as his predecessors, may be guaranteed such minutes as were taken by this Council on the 12th of January 1735, whereby the advocate fiscal was accorded the right to view and obtain copies of all such documents as he might require in his office, and therefore that the secretary may be ordered to provide the requested copies to His Excellency by virtue of the aforementioned minute dated the 12th of January 1735, as he requires them ex officio.

text_translated_detailed: No. 32. Wednesday the 3rd of October 1742, present the Noble Lord President, likewise the Lords Councilors and co-opted Members in this matter. In accordance with the Extract from the minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India of the 28th of the last month of September, on this day with the Noble Lord President of this Council having come above, the co-opted Member, the Honorable Karel Koenad, and after having spent a little time in the chamber, the same was requested to enter by the secretary, when His Honor having appeared in the assembly, the Oath for the office of Councilor of Justice, standing in the hands of the well-born Noble Lord President, was duly taken, and thereupon he took his seat next to the Honorable Jan Cornelis du Quesne, of which it is understood that this notation is to be kept and to be inserted in the memorial of the Council. [Understood.] In witness of me [was signed] G. Schuijlenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial of the Honorable Council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, dated as above. W. text_translated_detailed: No. 36. Saturday the 6th of October in the year 1742. Present the Noble Lord President, as well as the gentlemen Councilors and co-opted Members in this matter. After the handling of some points concerning the seized persons Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips, the Lord pro interim advocate fiscal of India Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma asked the Noble Lord President whether the extraordinary session would proceed on the coming Wednesday, as he wished to have some persons summoned to give testimony. Moreover, it having been noted that the adjunct sworn clerk Pieter Haksteen had raised difficulties regarding providing authenticated copies of the opinions to be sent as copies along with the citation to his Excellency, requesting that the said Haksteen be qualified for this purpose. Thereby it was discovered by this council that the said Lord pro interim advocate fiscal intended to issue ordinary citations against the gentlemen Mr. Bernhard Jacob Dellafaille, Mr. Pieter Willem Lammens, Mr. Theodorus Polycarpus Woijt, and Mr. Jean Blocquau, members of this council, as well as the Lord water fiscal Mr. Joan Hendrik van Panhuijs, to see what claims might be made. When the Noble Lord President, after the Lord pro interim advocate fiscal had been asked to give the council some freedom and had withdrawn to the adjoining chamber before taking any disposition in this matter, this council was given to consider that while the said Lord pro interim advocate fiscal intended to proceed with the case against the said gentlemen, it would not be safest to do so before first requesting clarification from the Noble High Government of these lands regarding the letter from the High Noble gentlemen the Seventeen in the homeland concerning what their Noble High Excellencies had deigned to order regarding the matter of the former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier with respect to the aforesaid gentlemen members, since the sentiments regarding this had been different at the previous Wednesday, but this was brought into question and deemed unnecessary.

text_translated_detailed: No. 42, Saturday the 13th of October in the year 1742. Present: the Noble Lord President, as well as the gentlemen Council members and assumed members herein. By the Noble Lord President of this Council, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, it was communicated to this Council today that yesterday, by the gentleman Willem Mauriets Bruijnink, on behalf of and in the name of the detained Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, a certain ample request had been presented to their High Nobility, the Noble High Government of these lands, tending toward the recusal both of the aforementioned Noble Lord President as well as the gentleman pro interim advocate fiscal, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, not only with regard to the aforementioned Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, but also with respect to the matter of the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier. Therefore, after due consideration by this Council, it has been deemed good to address their High Nobility and respectfully to request from them an authentic copy of the aforementioned request presented by the gentleman Bruijnink on behalf of and in the name of the detained member of this Council, Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, in order to proceed accordingly as shall be deemed advisable. Undersigned, in my knowledge, was signed G. Schuylenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial of the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, dated as above. D. text_translated_detailed: No. 44, Thursday the 18th of October 1742. Present: the Noble Lord President, as well as the gentlemen Council members and assumed members herein. By the gentleman pro interim advocate fiscal of India, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, there was brought to this Council today for communication a certain copy of a request presented by the gentlemen Mr. Bernard Jacob Dellafaille, Mr. Pieter Willem Lammens, Mr. Theodorus Policarpus Woijt, Mr. Jan Blocquau, and Mr. Johan Hendrik van Panhuijs to the Noble High Government of these lands, together with an extract from the minutes of what was dealt with and resolved in the Council of India on the 12th of this month, whereby the aforementioned gentleman pro interim advocate fiscal has been ordered to make his defense regarding what is contained in the aforementioned request with respect to his Honor, requesting the aforementioned gentleman pro interim advocate fiscal to be permitted to know whether this Council shall be pleased to involve itself in this matter and to supply his Honor thereupon with its Venerable advice for the substantiation and corroboration of his defense, which was his intention to exhibit in obedience to the commands of their High Nobility in the Council of India tomorrow. Because it was believed that the same request is absolutely a matter of justice and belonging to this Council, therefore, after reading of the one and the other, by majority of votes it was understood that his Honor's defense should be allowed to proceed as shall be deemed most advisable, and further to address their High Nobility at the earliest opportunity and to request that regarding the aforementioned request of the aforementioned gentleman Mr. Bernard Jacob Dellafaille, it not be disposed of, but rather, as it is a matter of justice, it may be referred to this Council for decision. Undersigned, in my knowledge, was signed G. Schuylenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial of the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, dated as above. D. Haksteen, Ed. Edck. Gesw. Clerc.

text_translated_detailed: No. 45½ Friday the 19th of October in the year 1742. Saturday the 27th of October 1742. Present the Noble lord president, likewise the lords Councillors and co-opted members herein. By the Noble lord president Mr. Jacob Lakeman [Lakeman:] was brought before the council today the following Extract from the minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India. Among the lords councillors for resumption it was found and having returned again, the request of Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius [Helvetius:] mentioned in the minutes of the 12th instant, so it was deliberated upon regarding the recusal requested thereby of the lord Mr. Jacob Lakeman and the interim advocate fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma [Jongsma:], both in his own matters and in the matters of his related brother the former lord governor-general Adriaan Valckenier [Valckenier:], it was deemed good and understood that the aforementioned Helvetius should address himself to the judge here regarding the recusal of the aforementioned lord president Lakeman as the ordinary way and to use the legal means thereto (noted below) was signed P.s A.s v.d.n Parra secretary. So after resumption thereof it was understood that the same should be inserted in the memorial of the council (noted below) In witness of which I (was signed:) G.s Schuijlenburg secretary). - Extracted from the memorial of the venerable council of justice of this Castle and agrees. text_translated_detailed: No. 48 Saturday the 24th of September 1742. Present the Noble Lord President, as well as the Lords Councillors and co-opted Members in this matter. Extract from the minutes of what was discussed and resolved in the Council of India, taken on Friday the 16th of this month, now communicated to this Council. It is hereby made known that the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier [Adriaan Valckenier:] from the Cape of Good Hope [Kaap de Goede Hoop:] has arrived here and has been brought to one of the bastions of the Castle in military arrest, in order to be treated according to the orders of Your Excellencies' High Regard, without it being established thereby what access to this person was granted by Your Excellencies to the same, or whether the withdrawal of this access was demanded of this Council. Thus, upon the difficulty raised by some of the Lords Members as to whether one might allow the same Lord Valckenier to continue to enjoy the aforementioned access, it was declared by the Noble Lord President that no one had been granted any access or entry to the aforementioned former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier by Your Excellencies, except only to the Noble Lord Councillor Extraordinary Nicolaes Caul, Mr. Willem Maurits Bruijning, and Mrs. the widow Massis. It was deemed good and agreed that for now no special decision should be taken in this matter, but to wait with it until the Lord Pro Interim Advocate Fiscal might come forward in this matter [understood:], in knowledge of me [was signed:] G. Schuijlenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial of the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, date as above. Haksten, Ad[vocaat] W[erf:] Gesrar Clercq No. 49

text_translated_detailed: No: 84 Esteemed Lords. — Brief Deduction, delivered to the Present Lords Councillors, and assumed Members herein, by the Extraordinary Councillor of India, and President of the Esteemed Council of Justice of this Castle, upon and against a certain Request of Recusal by the detained Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, both for himself and for the interest of his brother-in-law the lord former governor general Adriaen Valckenier, delivered to this Council and submitted. The undersigned president of the esteemed council of Justice of this castle, having read and summarized the aforesaid request, together with the means of yet another similar request to the high government of this land, delivered on the 12th of October previously, but there dismissed, shall note in general or for the present, that as the foundation of this request for the greatest part, the same means and reasons have again been employed, which have already been rejected by the council of Justice as unfounded upon the recusal of the lord Stapel, and must further hereby testify, that however gladly he in these troublesome times would wish to be relieved of the handling of this hateful matter, yet he cannot properly divest himself of a post to which he has bound himself by solemn oath, and in which he has been confirmed by his last promotion by the lords masters, notwithstanding that he has been fully informed of all of this, for it cannot be unknown to the undersigned and your esteemed selves, how burdensome and vexing it is to handle criminal procedures, particularly when the same must be undertaken against persons who are allied to respectable families, or who have held the highest dignities here in this land: and having received a substantial understanding of this from the very beginning, as soon as the lord former governor general Adriaen

text_translated_detailed: No. 85 Monday the 11th of December 1741. Present all members except in this case Mr. Helvetius;— on the occasion of today, by this council was resumed the minutes of the 6th of this month concerning the requisite demanded by resolution of their High Excellencies, the Noble high government of these lands from the first beforehand, so Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst has sustained and brought into consideration whether or not, to prevent needless quarrels and violent debates which concerning this matter not only had already occurred but also today were still taking place and further were to be expected, Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, both on account of the relationship with the repatriated Lord Governor-General Adriaen Valckenier [Adriaan Valckenier] as well as for other reasons, since in all dispositions and minutes in this matter he had always excused himself from giving his Excellency's vote, and also in advising the members ought not to be deprived of their freedom and to absent themselves, declaring the aforementioned Mr. van Reverhorst as then all the better positioned to be able to express his Excellency's opinion, whereupon the aforementioned Mr. Helvetius likewise sustained and brought to this council into consideration, whether the Noble Lord President Mr. Jacob Lakeman [Jacob Lakeman] then also ought not to be excused and excluded from giving his advice in this matter, while his Excellency had remained with the power of attorney from the Lord Gustaaf Willem van Imhoff [Gustaf Willem van Imhoff]. — so it was after careful consideration of the necessary matters by this council understood, that Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius should not only be further excused from his Excellency's advice in the matter of the repatriated Lord Governor-General Adriaen Valckenier [Adriaan Valckenier], but also his Excellency should be requested to absent himself from advising in this matter and to leave this council free

text_translated_detailed: A decision of Her High Excellencies, dated 26th November last, was brought to our knowledge, in which it was accepted for communication, and that the necessary orders would be issued; to grant no one access to the aforementioned former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier. And further, by the Pro interim advocate fiscal [prosecutor], by means of a written request on the first of December aforementioned, we were asked for the taking of hostage of the person of Pasquaal Andriesz: but which, after we had reviewed the documents, we were unable to grant, since from the supplied inquiry, not the slightest foundation was found for it, wherefore we denied that request. — just as we also on the 13th thereof, but for now have rejected the request of the old secretary of Her High Excellencies Willem Maurits Bruijnink, to be permitted to have access to his brother-in-law the aforementioned former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, since such was deemed untimely; and against the manner of proceeding was judged to be contrary; just as also on the same day upon an oral request made in the name of the Councillor Extraordinary Nicolaas Crul directed to that end, it was understood not to be disposed of. An Extract decision of Her High Excellencies, of the 27th November before, was brought to us some days prior, and on the aforementioned 13th December taken up for reading, together with the request by the aforementioned former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier presented for obtaining permission to act [Veniam agendi], against the President of this Council there, accompanied by some draft articles, in order to hear His Excellency thereupon, as well as the disposition concerning this unusual case, deferred and delivered to this Council by Her High Excellencies, we were unable to proceed to judge thereupon,

text_translated_detailed: No. 1 Saturday the First of December 1742. Present the Noble Lord President, likewise the Lords Councillors and Assumed Members therein. Through the pro interim advocate fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsman, the following request has been presented to the Council, and therewith the documents mentioned therein have been submitted, requesting as at the end of the same request. To the Well Noble Lord, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, Councillor Extraordinary of the Orders of the Netherlands India and President, together with the Esteemed Noble Lords Councillors and Assumed Members therein, your Excellency gives to know with reverence that Nicolaas Jongsman, pro interim advocate fiscal of the Netherlands India, that it is not only to the whole Batavian world and to your Excellency not unknown that the Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier has occupied himself daily in conferences with the well-known Pasqual Andries, but also that the latter has taken it upon himself to obtain and to conduct for this person and that person one or another lucrative office, as is not obscurely evident from the interrogations appended hereto, answered by the notary Vis Vliet, the hope-merchants Ferdinandus de Roij and Abraham Abbeleven, and the under-merchant Reijnier Harmens, and since the point of selling offices has been specially demanded for investigation by the Lords Masters, and he Pasqual Andries is moreover very suspect on account of his repeatedly sought removal from time to time in the house-renting, as the gang first lived just outside this city, subsequently on the road to Angiol, and has now already moved his residence to Janjongpriek, from where he could very easily escape to the great detriment of Justice, which the supplicant believes would be extraordinarily great through the loss of his person regarding the affairs of the aforementioned former Governor-General, for all which reasons, and since it is better to prevent than to provide a remedy after the wound is inflicted, as there is already an example of this in the case of the fugitive Halkenberg of Cabo de Goede

Op heeden door heeren Commissarissen ter Enqueste m:r Iacob Pompe van meerdervoort, en Karel Coenat aan desen raade zijnde overgegeven zeker berigt, waar bij onder andere quam te Consteeren dat den heer Justinus vinck drossaert den bataviase ommelanden voor haar agtb: gecompareert was, omme ter requisitie vanden heer pro interim advocaet fiscaal m:r Nicolaes Jongsma te beantwoorden Eenige articul en vraagpoincten, den selven als doen hadde gesustiteert op het Eerste articul den voorgehoudene vragen ongehouden te zijn te antwoorden en op het 20:' artl: gerespondeert dat hij op het gevraagde niet positieff konde antwoorden, alzoo het hem door de bankheijt des tijds ontschooten was, dat daar op gem: heer pao interim advocaet fiscaal zulx niet voldoende tevooren zynde gekoomen aangem: heeren commissarissen hadde versogt dat geciteerde heer Sustinus vinck mogte werden gecondemneert deselve articulen duijdelijken te beantwoorden 't welk haar agtb: hadde gehouden af referendum, soo is na overweging van het nodige bij desen raede verstaan het versoek door den heer proiijterim advocaet fiscaal aan heeren Commissarissen gedaen, te ontseggen, dogh egter niet temin zijn E: verheijt telaaten daar ontrent sodanige nadere articulen tot Elucidatie overteleggen, als raadsaem mogte oordeelen, zijnde te deser occagie door gem: heer prointemin advocaet
text_translated_detailed: No. 8. Thursday, the 13th of December 1742. Present the esteemed lord president, likewise the lords Councilors and co-opted members herein. On this day, by the lords Commissioners for Inquiry Mr. Jacob Pompe van Meerdervoort and Karel Coenat, a certain report was delivered to this council, whereby it came to be established among other things that the lord Justinus Vinck, drossard [chief magistrate] of the Batavian surroundings, had appeared before their Excellencies in order, at the requisition of the lord pro interim advocate fiscal Mr. Nicolaes Jongsma, to answer certain articles and question points. The same had then refused to answer the first article on the grounds of the question posed, and on the 20th article responded that he could not answer positively to what was asked, since it had escaped him due to the bankruptcy of the times. Whereupon the aforementioned lord pro interim advocate fiscal, finding this insufficient, had requested of the aforementioned lords commissioners that the cited lord Justinus Vinck might be condemned to answer the same articles clearly, which their Excellencies had held in abeyance. So, after consideration of what was necessary, this council understands that the request made by the lord pro interim advocate fiscal to the lords Commissioners is to be denied, but nevertheless His Excellency is permitted to submit such further articles for elucidation as might be deemed advisable, and on this occasion by the aforementioned lord pro interim advocate

text_translated_detailed: No. 10. Thursday the 13th of December 1742. Present the Noble Lord President, likewise the Lords Councillors and assumed Members herein. As now by the Noble Lord President Mr. Jacob Lakeman this council has been given into consideration, that since the inquiry was now sufficiently mostly concluded or the Lord pro interim advocate fiscal should not be enjoined within a certain peremptory time to proceed with the hostages Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips, together with the detained former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, to the end to hear them on articles, as being the two first mentioned having been placed in hostage since the 3rd of October and thereupon having been heard, the said pro interim advocate fiscal has thus declared that with regard to the two first mentioned he was indeed in a position now to begin, if this council would but be pleased to enjoin the same, yet that up to now he had not proceeded therewith on account of reasons by many hindrances known to his Lordship; he was prevented, and in particular because by their High Excellencies the recusation [challenge to a judge's impartiality] by the aforementioned Helvetius requested with regard to him and the named former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier there, although entirely absurd and unfounded, was not yet disposed of, and also his Excellency with respect to the last mentioned moreover sustained that he could not proceed therewith as yet, since with the ships expected to arrive various documents stood to come over

text_translated_detailed: No. 13 Thursday the 27th of December 1742. Present the Honorable Lord President; likewise the gentlemen Councilors and co-opted Members herein. Now, having taken up for review and examined with exactitude the answered question points supplied multiple times by the Lord Pro-interim Advocate Fiscal concerning the Chinese Tan Hiko, Souw Soeseeng, Lim Thoanko and the aforementioned Commissioner over the affairs of the Inlanders [indigenous peoples] Adriaan Subbels, as well as those of the Chinese Lim Tsouwko, Lim Hiensaij, Queliamko and Soeki-Etka, likewise those of the Lord Landdrost [district administrator] Justinus Vink, Admat Babandam, Mochamat Salé and Soeta Wangsa, the Pro-interim Advocate Fiscal made it known that although the misdeeds and extortions of the aforementioned Commissioner over the affairs of the Inlanders Ferdinandus De Roij appeared to him very probable and morally true, he nevertheless judged himself not yet authorized to make any request for incarceration or pledging in the Lord's prison against the same, for the reason that very many witnesses deposed matters heard secondhand or not directly witnessed, and frequently not without apparent passion, and moreover the aforementioned De Roij was in no way held to be suspect of the Suga [uncertain: original term], which the aforementioned Pro-interim Advocate Fiscal considered to be a requisite for such a request. text_translated_detailed: Saturday the 5th of January 1743. Present the Noble Lord President and the gentlemen Councillors and assumed members, on this day by the burgher Pieter Ingenhaag, both in the name of Maria Bas, wife of the merchant and former Commissioner for the affairs of the native Ferdinandus de Roij, as well as in the name of Ingenhaag and his wife Susanna Maurits, there was presented and signed to this council a certain request, and at the end thereof requested that they might be granted free access and entry to the aforementioned Ferdinandus de Roij, who was here pledged in the Lord's jail, but it being found that the same request contained among other things diverse singular, impudent, offensive and caustic expressions, as if this council had proceeded against law and equity with regard to the decreed pledging of the aforementioned de Roij, so in order to cut short such vile undertakings and to prevent them in the future, instead of disposing on the same request, the same shall be torn up by the secretary of this council after an authentic copy thereof shall first have been made, and thrown at the feet of the aforementioned Pieter Ingenhaag, and likewise the aforementioned Pieter Ingenhaag is to be condemned for presenting the same in a fine of two hundred rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch currency of the period] for the benefit of this Chamber, with interdiction from ever daring to submit such scandalous requests again, on pain that this council upon contravention against him Ingenhaag shall proceed with much more rigorous measures. Understood in knowledge of me, was signed G. Schuijlenburg, secretary. Extracted from the memorial of the honorable council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia the 1st of April 1743. text_original: 'tsedert het laast van 't Jaar 1736. den geinterrog: heeft gewoont gehad in desselvs thuijn op jacatra, komende op sijn best een a twee maal des weeks in't Casteel bij den gouverneur generaal adriaan Valkenier, dat hij in deselve thuijn verbleeven is tot den 8. october, wanneer smorgens baven tannabang bij de suykermolen pannagorang de eerste slaij teg:s de rebellige Chineesen was geschiet dat den geinterrog: daar op des avonds soekende sijn retracte te neemen in de stad in sijn woning staande op de groote revier doen ten tyd bewoont werdende door de heer Iean blocquau gekomen is voor de nieuw poort deser stad vindende alles in repenroer, mitsgaders de chineesen hoorende en sien de attacqueeren de stad in de zuijder voorstad en siende een sterke brand die den geinterrog: vermeenden binnen de stad te weesen, waar ontdaan synde hadde hy gesogt na een goed hem komende en was geraakt in de thuijn van de heer schepen trabe alwaer hij sterk sesthien Europianen die nagt heeft afgewagt den uijtslag derden gantschen nagt geduurt hebbende woede der Chineesen, dat hij des morgens van daarmet syn Charet weder gereeden zijnde na de nieuwpoort, deselve als nog heeft gesloten gevonden en op het openen gewagt tot omtrent negen uuren, wanneer hem door den oud schepen Thornton is gewaarschout dat wanneer hij binnen wilde wesen de water poort van 'tcasteel open was, dat daar op derwaerts is gereeden hebbende in de charet twee geladene pistoolen een d:o snaphaen mitsg:s op de zijde een houwer en in de hand een steekaad, dat in't casteel gekomen zijnde hij geg: sijn coetsier na huijs op de groote revier gesonden hadde met gem snaphaen en pistoolen en het overige geweir bij hem heeft gehouden mitsgaders in't casteel veel gevlugte vrouwen en geborgen goederen vindende ook aldaar is verbleeven
text_translated_detailed: since the end of the year 1736 the interrogated has dwelt in his own garden on Jacatra, coming at best one or two times a week to the Castle with the Governor-General Adriaan Valkenier, that he remained in the same garden until the 8th of October, when in the morning above Tannabang at the sugar mill Pannagorang the first clash against the rebellious Chinese had occurred, that the interrogated thereupon in the evening seeking to take his retreat into the city to his dwelling standing on the great river, then at that time being inhabited by the gentleman Jean Blocquau, came to the new gate of this city, finding everything in great disorder, and moreover hearing and seeing the Chinese attacking the city in the southern suburb and seeing a strong fire which the interrogated believed to be within the city, being alarmed by this he sought a good place for himself and was caught in the garden of the gentleman Schepen Trabe, where he strongly waited out that night with sixteen Europeans, the entire night having lasted with the fury of the Chinese, so that in the morning from there with his carriage having ridden again to the new gate, he found the same still closed and waited for its opening until about nine o'clock, when he was warned by the old Schepen Thornton that if he wished to be inside the water gate of the castle was open, that thereupon he rode there having in the carriage two loaded pistols, one of the same snaphaun [snaphance musket], and on the side a cutlass and in hand a dagger, that having come into the castle he sent his coachman home to the great river with the mentioned snaphaun and pistols and kept the remaining weapons with him, and moreover finding in the castle many fleeing women and secured goods, he also remained there

text_translated_detailed: No. 3. Wednesday the 9th of January 1743. Present the Noble Lord President, as well as the Lords Councillors and Assumed members herein, by the Lords Commissioners Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst and Mr. Reijnier Stapel, delivered this day in Council the following minutes: Monday the 7th of January 1743, present the Lords Commissioners, Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst and Mr. Reijnier Stapel. The pledged Mr. Willem Vincent Halvetius appeared this day before the aforementioned Lords Commissioners mentioned in the head of this document, coming from the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle, for the purpose of being heard, in accordance with the disposition of the aforementioned Venerable Lordships dated the 5th of this month, on certain articles and question points. Thus his Excellency has declared himself well prepared to obey the aforementioned honored disposition. However, since a request had been made to their High Excellencies, tending toward both the recusal of the Noble Lord President Mr. Jacob Lakeman as well as of the pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaes Jongsma, concerning which the aforementioned, namely the Honored Lord President, had seen the disposition taken thereupon by the aforementioned Council, yet regarding the sustained recusal against the pro interim Advocate Fiscal, he, Halvetius, had not yet seen the least decision thereupon, and therefore their Venerable Lordships in consideration whether there might flow from this in the meantime a nullity; further sustaining that his willingness to respond in no way could or should prejudice the Exceptions which the former Governor General Adriaan Valckenier might propose; and finally the aforementioned Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius requested that, since the words of the mandate by which he was enjoined not to alienate goods had been forgotten, and he would need money for the conduct of his household, that therefore the disposition of the cited mandate might once be read to him, for the purpose of being able to regulate himself accordingly, when by

text_translated_detailed: No. 4. On this day the 14th of January 1743. There appeared before the Lords Commissioners from the Venerable Council of Justice of the Castle Batavia, Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst and Mr. Rijnier Stapel, together with me Pieter Haksteen, adjunct sworn clerk of the aforementioned Venerable Lordships, the pledged and aforementioned person summoned hither, who, having been carefully heard on the content of the above interrogatories and his responses given thereto, remained thereby persisting with the following amplifications, namely as to article 7, that these were also not prisoners of Justice but war prisoners, rebels, and prisoners of the government; as to article 27, that the same person some time thereafter has related among other discourses that he had been jested with, that he had caused a Chinese person to be done away with by his boys under the pretext of harboring him, whereupon the aforementioned was then confronted by him with the statement that he should have followed the aforementioned's advice to hand over the Chinese to the Kaffirs, when it would still have been to be seen whether he would not have ended up in chains or escaped, and that at least then they would not have been able to plague him with it. Adding to article 32, further that after the general massacre on Sunday morning, whether begun and undertaken without or with orders, it was subsequently not reckoned as a crime by anyone to kill the remaining and here and there hidden Chinese in order to save their lives, just as this was done by all manner of people themselves in the sight of persons of the first rank and of lords members of the council in Batavia, so that the same in due time, if it shall be necessary, shall appear that on the requested 11th of September [8ber: uncertain: possibly "8ber" for "8 September" or similar], by the Noble High Indian government it was decided not only all wandering

text_translated_detailed: Saturday the 19th of January 1743. Present the Noble Lord President, as well as the Lords Councillors and Assumed members herein, by the Lords Commissioners Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst and Mr. Rijnier Stapel, there was delivered this day in Council the following minutes: Monday the 14th of January 1743, present the Lords Commissioners Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst and Mr. Rijnier Stapel. After on this day by the pledged Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius there had been recollected such articles and question points as by the same on the 7th of this month in the presence of the aforementioned Lords Commissioners mentioned in the head of this document have been answered, his Excellency requested to be able to have a copy both of the request upon which the pro interim advocate fiscal had granted the pledging of his person, as well as of the articles and his responses given thereto, founding his request on the unanimous doctrine of all criminalists and constant practice observed before all courts of justice, and especially of the High Council of Holland, Zeeland, and West Friesland, and of the Venerable Council of Justice of this castle, further referring as a foundation of this request to the doctrine of Mr. Pieter Borst in his treatise on criminal matters, title 5, number 49, in

text_translated_detailed: Saturday the 19th of January 1743. Present the Noble Lord President, the Lords Councillors and co-opted Members herein. By the Noble Lord President there was brought before the Council today the following Extract from the minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India. Tuesday the 15th of January 1743. — Subsequently it was deemed good that the two secret letters by the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier addressed to the High Noble Lords Seventeen [the governing body of the VOC in Amsterdam] were registered and by the said High Noble Lords, together with the attached documents, were sent back here according to the tenor of their letter of the 13th of December 1741, to be delivered to the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle (undersigned:) agreed (was signed:) P.A. van der Parre, Secretary. So after this resumption and after the two secret letters mentioned therein were read before this Council, it was understood that the same should be delivered to the Lord pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, together with the above Extract to be inserted in the memorial of this Council (undersigned:) in witness of me (was signed:) G. Schuijlenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial of the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle and agrees. Batavia, dated as above. Baksteen [uncertain: possibly a name or title]. H. Gesur Clercq. Ad. Saturday the 19th of January 1743, present the Noble Lord President, and the Lords Councillors and co-opted Members herein. By the Noble Lord President there was brought before the Council today the following. Extract from the minutes of what was deliberated and resolved in the Council of India. Tuesday the 15th of January in the year 1743. At the session of the 19th of December of the past year, which had been postponed, there remained to be decided the disposition on the second point of the petition made by the now imprisoned ordinary Member in the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius [normalized version: William Vincent Helvetius] for the recusal of the pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, both in the matter of himself and his brother-in-law the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, so it was now deemed good and understood that the said Helvetius should address himself to that end to the aforementioned Council, and leave the disposition concerning this to the same. Undersigned: Agrees, and was signed P. van der Parre, Secretary. So after this resumption it was understood that the same should be inserted in the memorial of this Council. Undersigned: In witness of me, and was signed G. Schuijlenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial...

At the session of the 19th of December of the past year, which had been postponed, there remained to be decided the disposition on the second point of the petition made by the now imprisoned ordinary Member in the Venerable Council of Justice of this Castle Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius for the recusal of the pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, both in the matter of himself and his brother-in-law the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, so it was now deemed good and understood that the said Helvetius should address himself to that end to the aforementioned Council, and leave the disposition concerning this to the same. Undersigned: Agrees, and was signed P. van der Parre, Secretary. So after this resumption it was understood that the same should be inserted in the memorial of this Council. Undersigned: In witness of me, and was signed G. Schuijlenburg, Secretary. Extracted from the memorial...

Saturday the 19th of January 1743. Present the Noble Lord President, and the Lords Councillors and co-opted Members herein. By the here pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaes Jongsma there was presented to the Council today the following request, and thereupon submitted a register with various documents, requesting as at the end of the same request:

To the Noble Lord Mr. Jacob Lakeman, Councillor Extraordinary of the Netherlands Indies and President, together with the further Lords and co-opted Members of the Venerable Council of Justice of the Castle Batavia.

Noble Lord and Venerable Lords, the pro interim Advocate Fiscal of the Netherlands Indies Mr. Nicolaes Jongsma hereby shows you in the register sub No. 1 and 2 a certain act of imprisonment and thereupon attached disposition dated the 3rd of October of the past year, together with various articles and question points answered by the Merchant Henry Abbis, E.S., of the 2nd thereof, marked No. 3, whereby and according to which Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, ordinary Member in the aforementioned Council, under the supervision of a bailiff and clerk, was imprisoned provisionally in his own dwelling, and furthermore the same was interdicted from alienating any goods and papers under such penalty as Your Excellency and Venerable Lords shall understand to be fitting. That subsequently at the requisition of the undersigned, the said Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius was heard on certain admitted points hereupon marked No. 4, and answered the same, together with what was recollected, it has become entirely clear that far from bringing forward anything substantial for his exoneration, on the contrary he is found guilty of such unheard-of and pernicious other crimes, as by reading found and in the continuation of this document will be mentioned: it is true that the same has attempted to prove the first point of the horrible and heaven-crying...

text_translated_detailed:
No. 13. Wednesday, the 8th of February 1743. Present: the Honorable Lord President, the Lords Councillors, and the assumed Members in this department, the Lord Vonglan being absent on Commission to Cheribon. For the aforementioned Council, Nicolaas Smit has, in the name and on behalf of the detained Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, delivered to the Council the following request:

To the Noble and Esteemed Lord Mr. Jacob Lakeman, Councillor Extraordinary of the Netherlands Indies and President, together with the Esteemed Lords Councillors of Justice of the Castle Batavia.

Noble and Esteemed Lords, I respectfully make known that Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, Ordinary Councillor of Justice of the Castle Batavia, now detained, that he, the supplicant, at the requisition of the Lord Mr. Nicolaas Iongsma, pro-interim Advocate Fiscal of the Netherlands Indies, in accordance with a certain appointment of Your Honors and Esteemed Commissioners Mr. Theodorus van Reverhorst and Mr. Reijnier Stapel issued on the 7th of January last, has been heard upon certain interrogatory articles. And after having answered categorically thereupon, on the 14th before the same well-mentioned Lords Commissioners in the presence of the aforementioned Lord pro-interim Advocate Fiscal, it was received that he, the supplicant, after the conclusion of the aforementioned examination, requested to be able to have a copy both of the request upon which the Lord Winter, Advocate Fiscal, granted the detention of the supplicant's person, as well as of the aforementioned interrogatories and given responses, on the foundation of certain learned legal authorities and firm rules of the universally prevailing practice. That the well-mentioned Lords Commissioners, deliberating upon the supplicant's request, have deemed it good to tell the supplicant that he must make the aforementioned request to the Council. That the supplicant thereupon became of the opinion to postpone the same request for such time until the Lord, formerly Governor General Valckenier, might also be heard upon articles, in the belief that thereby many positive statements made by the supplicant in his answers

text_translated_detailed: Just as was mentioned before, on Tsilinsing in 1740, when he arrived there in the presence of the same, several praaus [small boats] were requisitioned and other overseers with one of their respective boatmen were detained. A large number of praaus with their respective reasons—since they had no passes—were detained. It is stated that the overseers Salem and one of his fellow overseers were present there at Gadje. It is stated that there were two praaus and two boatmen; how many prau boatmen and praaus. To whose order this occurred. Or whether the same did not occur by order of the king.—It fails, it fails because the same had no passes. On what pretext and for what reason the detention occurred, it is stated that the praaus were on the Silinsing, where the people and their belongings lay, and the folk were brought and conveyed away with small items, brought without yet now knowing by whom. It is stated not to know that the same were firmly held, nor in what manner they were again released, and also not that the same were again released. Or whether they had to pay no money for it. It fails, how much. To whom or to whose order or the requisitioned. Regarding this, something more is known. text_translated_detailed: Lord President, and the Gentlemen Councilors and Assumed Members present in this matter, being the Lord van Glan in Commission to Cheribon, by the pledged person has been presented to the Council the following request with the request as in the end thereof.—To the Noble Lord, Mr. Jacob Lakeman, Councilor Extraordinary of Dutch India and President. Together with the Further Gentlemen Members of the Honorable Council of Justice of this Castle.—Noble Lord and Honorable Gentlemen, Ferdinandus de Roij, merchant in the service of the Company, gives to Your Honor and Respectability to know with deep and dutiful respect that he, the supplicant, on the 27th of December of the recently passed year, by order of Your Honor and Respectability, was brought into pledging within the Company's boathouses, and now recently at the requisition of the Lord pro interim Advocate Fiscal of India, Mr. Nicolaes Jongsma, in the presence of the Gentlemen Commissioners from this Honorable Council, concerning various points and matters which he, the supplicant, both from former rumors as from the articles put forward, must establish that his enemies alone and solely have invented and spread about, in order, if it were possible, to make him, the supplicant, unfortunate, and to cause Your Honor and Respectability, saving your reverence, to form a mistaken opinion against him. On a multitude of articles and question points he, the supplicant, has been heard, which he, the supplicant, trusts will not only never and in eternity be able to be shown and proven to the satisfaction of the judge, but moreover also that Your Honor and Respectability and the whole world, upon careful examination and reading of the same, will immediately be convinced of his innocence regarding what is laid to his charge, as well as of the untruth, fabricated falsehoods and inventions, and of never thought of, much less committed misdeeds. Wherefore he, the supplicant, takes the liberty hereby to turn to Your Honor and Respectability with humble request and plea, to the end that—

text_translated_detailed: No. 21. Monday, the 4th of March, Anno 1743. — Present: The Noble Lord President, likewise the Lords Councilors and co-opted Members present herein, being the Lord van Glan on Commission to Cheribon. Regarding the presented request of the detained Ferdinandus de Roij, the Advocate Fiscal Pro Interim having declared that His Excellency consented with respect to the first part of that request and further found it profitable to accept the offered surety for the detained person's person in such manner as is more broadly expressed in the second part of that request, so, notwithstanding that the same declaratory seemed to this Council quite speculative and strange, it was understood to pay no regard to the latter, and consequently to deny the second part of the request of the detained de Roij as premature, yet at the same time seriously recommending to the aforementioned Advocate Fiscal Pro Interim to observe his office and duty concerning the matter of de Roij. text_translated_detailed: No. 23. Tuesday, the 5th of March 1743. Present: The Noble Lord President, likewise the Lords Councilors and co-opted Members present herein, being the Lord von Glan on Commission to Cheribon. By the hereinafter named Commissioners, there was brought before the Council today the following Minute: Tuesday, the 5th of March 1743. Present: the Lords Commissioners van den Bosch and van Reverhoust. The aforementioned Lords Commissioners, together with the Lord Advocate Fiscal Pro Interim, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, and the secretary, pursuant to the decision of yesterday, having proceeded to the former Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, now detained, in order to hear him upon the exhibited articles at the requisition of the aforementioned Advocate Fiscal Pro Interim, the detained person declared that he was indeed willing to answer the articles presented to him, provided that thereby his right was not curtailed, since the detained person maintains that he belongs under the Council of States by virtue of Amsterdam parents, and indeed of such as have been Regents of the aforementioned city for the past two to three hundred years, from which he is descended. Whereupon the Lords Commissioners, wishing to proceed with the presentation of the articles, the detained person sustained that the foregoing ought first to be decided by the Council, and on the foundation thereof expressly refused to answer.

Present De Heeren Commissarissen van Den Bosch en Reverhorst Den Gedetineerden Gewesen heere Gouverneur Generaal Adriaan Valckenier gerecolert hebbende soodanig art:l en vraegpoincten als door denzelven op den 6: 7:' 8:' en 9:' deser tenoverstaen van den in den hoofde deses genoemde heeren Commiss=n zijn beandwoord, soo versogte Gem: heere Valckenier te mogen Erlangen Copia soo van zijne geproponeerd hooger beroep aan de Raad van staten ende daar opgevallene Dispositie, als van de articulen en vraeg poincten, sijne daar op gegevene responsiven, en daar agterstaende recollement, mitsgaders dat aen hem wegens zijne indispositie mogte werden gepermitteerd Een procureur te gebruijken omme sijne defensie te doen welke versoeken bij haar agtbaarheedens genomen zijnde in deliberatie soo is verstaen deselve te neemen adreferendum /:onderstond:/ In kennisse van mij /:was getekend:/ p:s Schuijlenburg secret=s Zoo is nadies resumtie gelet sijnde op de versoeken van den gedetineerde Heer Adriaan Valckenier daar bij vervat, mitsg=s gehoord hebbende het declaratoir van den heer Pro-Interim Ad vocaet Fiscael verstaen de Twee Eerst gem: versoeken te accordeeren en dien volgende aen hem te verleenen Copia zoo van zijn geproponeerde hooger beroep aende raad van staaten ende daar op gevallene dispositie als vande articulen en vraagpoincten zijne/ daer op gegevene responsiven en het daer agterstaende recollement
text_translated_detailed: No. 27 Monday the 25th of March 1743. Present the Honorable lord President. Also the gentlemen Counselors and assumed members in this matter. Excepting the lord Kien due to indisposition and the lord Vonglan as being on Commission to Cheribon. By the undersigned gentlemen Commissioners on this day delivered. The following minutes. Monday the 18th of March 1743. Present the Gentlemen Commissioners van Den Bosch and Reverhorst. The Detainee, former lord Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, having collated such articles and question points as by the same on the 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th of this month before the gentlemen Commissioners named in the head of this have been answered, so the aforementioned lord Valckenier requested to be able to obtain a copy both of his proposed higher appeal to the Council of States and the disposition that resulted therefrom, as well as of the articles and question points, his responses given thereto, and the collation following thereupon, moreover that to him on account of his indisposition might be permitted to use a procurator [legal representative] to conduct his defense, which requests being taken by their venerableships into deliberation, so it is understood that the same be taken ad referendum [for further consideration]. Witnessed by me [was signed] p.s Schuijlenburg secretary. Thus, after this resumption having been considered upon the requests of the detainee lord Adriaan Valckenier contained therein, moreover having heard the declaration of the lord Pro-Interim Advocate Fiscal, it is understood that the two first-mentioned requests are to be granted and accordingly to him to be granted a copy both of his proposed higher appeal to the Council of States and the disposition that resulted thereupon as well as of the articles and question points his responses given thereto and the collation following thereupon.

text_translated_detailed: No. 28. Monday the 25th of March 1743, present the Honorable Lord President, and the gentlemen Councilors and co-opted Members, in which the Lord Kien is absent due to indisposition and Lord von Glans on commission to Cheribon. By the Lord pro interim Advocate Fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, the following request has been presented to the Council on this day, and therewith submitted the disposition mentioned therein: requesting, as at the end of the said request: To the Honorable Lord Mr. Jacob Lakeman, Councilor Extraordinary of the Dutch Indies and President, together with the further Lords and co-opted Members of the — : esteemed Council of Justice of the Castle Batavia. Honorable Lord and esteemed Lords, the pro interim Advocate Fiscal of the Indies, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma (: in consideration of the reasons and means alleged by him in the herewith presented request and by the disposition standing behind it of Your Honor and Esteemed [Lords] dated the 19th of January of this year, whereby two requests for marceration [uncertain: marceration] upon the person, together with arrest, inventory, and sequestration of the goods of the now detained Mr. Willem Vincent Selvetius have been denied for the time being, takes the liberty hereby with due respect to make known that he, according to his limited knowledge and understanding, has been unable to discern any reasons for the aforesaid denial, unless Your Honor and Esteemed [Lords] might have been moved thereto because the same at that time had not had full knowledge of the memorial [uncertain: n sive] drawn up by the detained [person] and sent by the former Governor General Adriaan Valkenier to the Lords Majores, or else because the latter, as then, had not yet been heard and was not in confession, concerning the complicity and the trampling upon the detained [person] in and concerning the undertaken and on the 6th of December 1740 in an unheard-of manner executed arrest, of three ordinary Members out of the representative sovereigns of these Lands.

Monday the 25th of March 1743, present the Honorable Lord President, and the gentlemen Councilors and co-opted Members in this, excepting the Lord Kien due to indisposition and Lord Vonglan on commission to Cheribon. The pro interim Advocate Fiscal of the Netherlands Indies, Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma, presents hereby to Your Honor and Esteemed [Lords] with due respect the Articles: by the former Governor General Adriaan Valkenier, now detained, on the 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th of this [month], answered, but in such a manner that the same has far from satisfied the disposition of this Council dated the 4th before, herewith annexed, and containing a condemnation to answer thereupon categorically, that is according to Book Title 9, No. 6 and 7, and the order on the style of procedure, Article 13, merely by yes or no, of which Your Honor and Esteemed [Lords] will find the contrary, and Articles 3, 4, 8, 9, 62, 84, 85, 88, 89, 90, 91, 92, 93, 97, 98, 99, 107, 119, 122, 135, 137, 143, 158, 160, 203, 204, 243, 244, 245, 246, 247, 248, 254, 255, 256, 257, 267, 272, and 290; so that the aforementioned Fiscal finds himself authorized and necessitated hereby most earnestly and respectfully to request that Your Honor and Esteemed [Lords], on the foundation as well of your aforementioned disposition as of the style and manner of procedure, deign to condemn the detained [person] and to order him to answer further and yet again categorically to the articles specified herein. The Council, having given careful consideration to the exhibited answers and recollected articles, and disposed upon the above request, denies the same /:understood:/ In witness of me /was signed:/ G. Schuijlenburg, secretary. Extracted from the Criminal hall of the esteemed Council of Justice of this Castle and accords. Batavia, date as above. [uncertain: Hbaksteen] Adr. Gesw. Clercq.

text_translated_detailed: To Your Honors and Esteemed Gentlemen with due respect, Nicolaas Crul, Councilor Extraordinary of the Netherlands Indies, and Colonel of the Batavian Burgher militia, that the Lord Former Governor-General of India Adriaan Valkenier, before his departure from here in the year 1741, constituted the Supplicant together with the Gentlemen Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Johannes van der Linde as his general attorneys, in order to conduct and oversee all his Honors' affairs and business here, and at the same time the Supplicant was appointed as Cashier and the aforementioned Lord Helvetius as keeper of the charters and papers. By virtue of which the Supplicant has indeed the demanded Administration of the received monies, and the aforementioned Lord Helvetius who obtained the aforementioned Charters and papers and have held them for a long time. But since the aforementioned Lord Helvetius, by order of this Esteemed Council, has been placed under arrest or detention in this Council's house, with an interdiction to remove anything from his house or to pledge it, and there are various obligations and debt letters in favor of the aforementioned Lord Former Governor-General Valkenier and charged against diverse Chinese, which remain in his possession, which the Supplicant, by the right of his equal Principal, both by instituting action on the insolvent estates of this one and that one of the debtors, for which the Supplicant has already been summoned in his aforementioned capacity, as otherwise to oversee, so he is compelled hereby to address himself to Your Honors and Esteemed Gentlemen with respectful request in order that the aforementioned Lord Helvetius may be permitted, or indeed qualified, to deliver all the obligations and debt letters which under his Honor in the aforementioned capacity for the benefit of the aforementioned Lord Former Governor-General and charged against diverse Chinese remain in his possession, to him, the Supplicant. text_translated_detailed: No: 36. Wednesday the 27th of March 1743. Present the Noble Lord President, likewise the gentlemen councillors and co-opted members herein, excepting the Lord Kien who is indisposed, the Lord Vonglan being on commission to Cheribon [Cirebon]. Today, pursuant to the notarial resolution of the 25th of this month, there has been received the written declaratory statement of the Lord pro interim advocate fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Iongsma [Jongma] upon and against the request presented by the detained Mr. Cornelis Phillips on the 25th of this month aforesaid to this council, and at the same time therein certain counter-requests at the end of the same declaratory statement made by the said Lord pro interim advocate fiscal Mr. Nicolaas Iongsma. The pro interim advocate fiscal of India, having been heard upon the aforesaid request, states that he, before declaring himself upon the multitude of requests made at the end thereof, must bring to the knowledge of Your Excellencies and Worships that to him, besides and apart from diverse mocking and very poorly applicable expressions and reasonings, the same request appears not only with regard to him fiscal, but even also with respect to Your Excellencies and Worships so in the recent so suggestive and so calumnious a manner, that the request presented some few years ago by the famous Ioan De Mauregnault to this council, it is to be noted, principally the person of the petitioner who was at that time still an ordinary member in this council, and according to reliable information appointed advocate fiscal to that impertinent purpose of his, and by the executioner in his presence torn to pieces, does not even come close, as that from No: 36.
